references.text: The angels commanded Lot to flee to the mountains, but Lot asked to go to Zoar instead. In verse 30 he finally leaves Zoar in fear and does what the angels originally said – he goes up into the mountains.
The continuation of the story: Lot's daughters take the initiative in the cave, which leads to the birth of Moab and Ben-Ammi, the ancestors of the Moabites and Ammonites.
Lot chose the fertile Jordan plain and settled near Sodom. His final dwelling in a mountain cave stands in sharp contrast to this initial choice.
Lot was taken captive while living in Sodom, showing his long-standing connection to the Sodom area before its final destruction and escape.
Lot originally set out from Ur together with Terah and Abram, marking the beginning of the journey that eventually led him to Sodom and then to the cave in the mountains.
